newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa hosts meeting on Great Lakes crisis.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hosts meeting on Great Lakes crisis.

text.p: African foreign ministers arrived in South Africa on Monday for crisis talks on the conflict in central Africa, where Zaire's army has begun a battle to regain rebel-held territory.

"The meeting is taking place after new allegations of further massacres in Burundi and at a time when the Zairean government has announced the launching of its counter-offensive in eastern Zaire," a foreign ministry statement said.

Ministry spokesman Marco Boni said the foreign ministers of South Africa, Kenya, Congo, Tanzania and Zimbabwe, and the deputy minister from Cameroon, would hold a brainstorming session late on Monday, then put their ideas to heads of state.
"It will probably be a precursor to a summit," he said.
A second regional summit on the crisis in December asked the group of ministers, led by Kenya, to take charge of efforts to end one of Africa's worst crises for years.

Rebels seized Zaire's eastern borderlands late last year, sparking an exodus of more than a million Hutu refugees from the camps they had lived in since fleeing Rwanda in 1994 to escape retribution for the genocide of up to 800,000 people.
Hutu refugees from Tutsi-controlled Burundi fled with them.
The rebellion sent giant Zaire, already unstable, deeper into chaos. Its government has now hired mercenaries to help it.
"The South African government views these developments, as well as the alleged mercenary involvement in the region, with increasing concern," the ministry said.
"The government is however confident the meeting of foreign ministers in Pretoria could make a considerable contribution to ensuring an early end to conflicts in the Great Lakes region."
Africa's largest private armed force, South African-based Executive Outcomes, denies it is involved in Zaire.

President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, denying a Sunday newspaper claim that it helped the firm win a contract with Angola four years ago, said it fully backed planned legislation to curb mercenary activities.
